messages.subject: color and fill
parts:
According to the common statement
"The difference between color and fill is that (for two dimensional
geoms) fill is the inside color and color is the outside color."

I should get different colors for the borders of the signs with this

ggplot(iris, aes(x = Petal.Length, y = Sepal.Length)) +
ggtitle("Iris Data") + geom_point(aes(color=Species,shape=Species),size=5)

and different filling colors with this

ggplot(iris, aes(x = Petal.Length, y = Sepal.Length)) +
ggtitle("Iris Data") + geom_point(aes(fill = Species,shape=Species),size=5)


Why am i geting different filling colors with the first command and
all black symbols
with the second one?

Thanks

Agus

messages.author: 146c5031f31e4913
messages.subject: Re: color and fill
parts:
Agus, 

The main problem is that the default plotting shapes for geom_point do not have a "fill" component. If you take a look at ?aes_linetype_size_shape in R or go here for the html version. Looking at the very last example shows that only shapes 21 through 25 take both colour and fill. 

To see this try my modifications to your examples

ggtitle("Iris Data") + geom_point(aes(fill = Species), size=5, shape = 21)

After changing the plotting shape to 21, colour changes the borders and fill changes the interior colour, just as you described. 

It is also possible to leave the variables mapped to both fill (or colour) and shape simultaneously, but then you'll also need to set the scale manually to shapes that have the additional fill component.

ggtitle("Iris Data") + geom_point(aes(fill = Species, shape = Species), size=5) +
  scale_shape_manual(values = c(21, 23, 25))

Thank you for posting a reproducible example.

Jake
